audit.originality: All prompts, contexts and figure briefs are original and derived from the controlled outcome rather than official question wording.
audit.scope: Qualitative gap-width-to-wavelength diffraction and demonstrations only; interference, coherence, fringes and grating equations are excluded.
audit.evidence: The canonical mapping records a genuine gap: no primary-mapped P2 leaf currently covers this outcome.

evidence.role: Direct retrieval from verified Lesson 5; current outcome has no primary-mapped P2 leaf.

hints: Include both the change to the wave and the boundary features where it happens.
walkthrough: Recall the complete controlled statement: diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle.

ai_rubric.observable: States that diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle

evidence.role: Original outcome-based qualitative comparison; no primary P2 mapping exists.

hints: Compare the opening with one wavelength, not with an everyday idea of small or large.
walkthrough: Marked spreading occurs when the gap width is comparable with the wavelength. A gap about equal to the wavelength fits this condition, so B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, a gap about equal to the wavelength

evidence.role: Original fixed-gap wavelength comparison; no primary P2 mapping exists.

hints: The gap stays fixed. Decide which wavelength is closer to its width.
walkthrough: At one fixed gap, the longer wavelength is more comparable with the gap width and gives more spreading. Therefore A is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects A, the longer-wavelength set spreads more at the fixed gap

evidence.role: Original experimental-control demand from the syllabus outcome; no primary P2 mapping exists.

hints: To isolate the effect of gap width, change only that variable.
walkthrough: Keep wavelength fixed and change only gap width so any change in spreading can be linked to gap width. Therefore C is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C, keep wavelength fixed and change only gap width

evidence.role: Original ripple-tank wavefront comparison for an outcome with no primary P2 mapping.

hints: Compare each labelled gap with the unchanged spacing of adjacent wavefronts.
walkthrough: Gap P is about one wavelength wide, whereas Q is several wavelengths wide. P therefore gives more strongly curved fronts and sends waves farther into side regions.

hints: Choose the gap closer to one wavefront spacing.
walkthrough: Gap P is comparable with the wavelength, so it produces more strongly curved emerging fronts.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies gap P as producing more strongly curved wavefronts

hints: Use both comparisons: P with wavelength and Q with wavelength.
walkthrough: P is comparable with one wavelength and so shows marked diffraction. Q is several wavelengths wide and so shows less overall spreading.

ai_rubric.observable: States that gap P is comparable with the wavelength
Links the comparable sizes to stronger diffraction than at the several-wavelength-wide gap Q

hints: Think about regions beside the direct straight-through route.
walkthrough: Stronger diffraction carries the wave farther into the side or geometric-shadow regions and across a wider range of directions.

ai_rubric.observable: States that waves reach farther into side or geometric-shadow regions, or cover a wider range of directions

evidence.role: Original practical-method demand from the controlled outcome; no primary P2 mapping exists.

hints: Organise the method as source, controls, changed variable and observation.
walkthrough: Make straight waves in a ripple tank. Keep depth and vibrator frequency fixed to keep wavelength fixed. Change only the adjustable gap width, then compare outgoing curvature or sideward spread. Reducing the gap toward one wavelength increases spreading.

hints: State what remains fixed, what changes and what is observed.
walkthrough: Produce straight wavefronts and hold water depth and vibrator frequency fixed. Change only the adjustable gap width. For every width, observe or trace outgoing wavefront curvature or sideward spread.

ai_rubric.observable: Produces straight wavefronts and keeps wavelength fixed, for example by keeping water depth and vibrator frequency fixed
Changes only the width of an adjustable gap
Compares outgoing wavefront curvature or sideward spread for the different widths

hints: Move from a gap many wavelengths wide toward a comparable size.
walkthrough: As the gap approaches one wavelength, the emerging fronts become more curved and spread across more directions.

ai_rubric.observable: States that reducing the gap toward one wavelength increases curvature or spreading

evidence.role: Prior diffraction recognition mixed with current relative-scale reasoning; current outcome has no primary P2 mapping.

hints: First name edge spreading, then compare each wavelength with the unchanged doorway.
walkthrough: The edge behaviour is diffraction. X has the longer wavelength, which is more comparable with the doorway width, so X spreads more. Y still diffracts, but its shorter wavelength gives less noticeable spreading.

hints: Recall the name for wave spreading around an obstacle edge.
walkthrough: The wave reaches around the edge by diffraction.

hints: The doorway is fixed, so compare the two wavefront spacings with it.
walkthrough: Panel X has the longer wavelength and is more comparable with the doorway width. Its waves therefore spread more strongly.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies panel X as showing more spreading
Explains that the longer wavelength is more comparable with the fixed doorway width

hints: Separate whether diffraction occurs from how noticeable it is.
walkthrough: Both wave sets spread at the edge and therefore both diffract. The shorter wavelength is smaller relative to the doorway, so its spreading is less noticeable rather than absent.

ai_rubric.observable: States that both wavelength sets diffract at the doorway edge
Explains that the shorter wavelength gives less noticeable rather than zero diffraction because it is smaller relative to the doorway
